title: Quiet Hours
summary: An editorial poster study in muted bronze and stone — built around a single horizon and restrained type.
fullDescription: Quiet Hours explores negative space as structure. The composition keeps the viewer at a measured distance, using a low horizon and sparse typography to create stillness rather than spectacle.
narrative: The piece began as a question about how little a poster needs to hold attention — and how silence can become the subject.

story.idea: Reduce a poster to horizon, mark, and type — then stop before the composition becomes decorative.
story.inspiration: Evening light on stone walls, museum wall labels, and the pause between gallery rooms.
story.process: Studies moved from dense sketches to progressively emptier frames until the horizon carried the weight of the page.

processSteps.title: Field studies
processSteps.description: Collected quiet interiors and low horizons, noting where the eye rested without instruction.

processSteps.title: Type restraint
processSteps.description: Tested title placements until the lettering supported the stillness instead of competing with it.

processSteps.title: Final balance
processSteps.description: Removed secondary marks until only horizon, accent, and title remained.

story.challenges: Knowing when emptiness was intentional rather than unfinished — every removed element had to earn its absence.
story.reflection: Restraint is not a lack of ideas. It is a decision about which ideas the viewer should carry away.

seo.metaDescription: An editorial poster study in muted bronze and stone by Rodge Andru.
